name: DCF-Calculator-Aesthetic
description: A DCF valuation you can actually read. Clean, interactive alternative to Excel DCF templates: live value per share, locked reported figures, bear case and sensitivity grid.

paragraphs: A DCF you can actually read. Same math as the spreadsheet, without the wall of grey cells.

Most DCF models live in Excel templates: hundreds of cells, tiny fonts, blue-for-input and black-for-formula, and a value per share buried somewhere around row 60. You can build them, but it's hard to show one to anyone. In a pitch or a meeting, people want to know three things: what is it worth, how does that compare to the price, and what would have to be true for the price to make sense.

Nothing is lost in the translation. The four bundled models match their source spreadsheets to the cent, and you can import any workbook built on the same template. Open it in your browser; there's nothing to install.
features: The answer is at the top. Value per share, the market price, and how far apart they are, in large type the second the page opens.

Only the judgment calls are editable. Reported figures and market prices are locked, so nobody "fixes" the revenue by accident. Growth, margins, discount rate and terminal assumptions are the knobs, each with a note on…

Every step is spelled out. Cash flows, plus terminal value, gives enterprise value; less net debt gives equity value; divided by shares gives the price. One clean list, not a chain of cell references.
It answers "what does the price assume?" It works out the long-run margin the market price needs, so a debate about whether a stock is cheap becomes a debate about one number.
Stress-testing takes one click. A bear case button, a reset button, and a sensitivity grid that marks the cell nearest today's price.

whatItDoes.text: A DCF you can actually read. Same math as the spreadsheet, without the wall of grey cells.

requirements.text: There is no server and no account, and nothing you type or import is uploaded anywhere.
